entry.title: Task Manager Pause Button 1.0.0
entry.content:
Task Manager Pause Button

Add a native Pause / Resume button next to Run new task in the Windows 11 Task Manager on the Processes and Details pages.

How to use

  1. Open Task Manager and select Processes or Details.
  2. Click Pause to stop the list from updating.
  3. Click Resume to start updating again.

The button controls Task Manager's refresh hold on Processes and Details. The mod does not suspend apps, stop Windows processes, or change the Real time update speed setting.

Compatibility and limitations

  • Works with the Windows 11 Task Manager XAML interface. Windows updates may change private Task Manager functions or controls.
  • Uses Task Manager's Ctrl-key refresh hold through GetKeyState calls made directly by Taskmgr.exe. While paused, some Task Manager keyboard actions may behave as if Ctrl is held, including Run new task (Ctrl+click can open Command Prompt instead of the normal dialog). This does not affect other apps.
  • Recognizes the tested Task Manager command-bar layout independently of display language: one command bar with four native buttons, with Run new task in the first position. Falls back to English/Portuguese labels or recognizable control identifiers on other layouts. Other Windows versions can have different layouts, so all languages/builds are not guaranteed.
  • Pause/Resume labels are in English regardless of the Task Manager language.
  • Keeps Pause active when moving between Processes and Details. Automatically resumes when navigating to another page if the navigation-exit symbol is available on your Windows build.
  • If the button is missing, close and reopen Task Manager with the mod enabled.
  • No settings or background applications are needed.

Source and feedback

GitHub

Author: Luiz Bizzio. License: Apache-2.0.

entry.title: Quick Look 1.0.0
entry.content:
Quick Look

A native Quick Look preview for Windows File Explorer, packed as a Windhawk mod.

Select a file or a folder and press Space. That is the whole idea.

Quick Look docks a real panel inside the File Explorer window, next to the file list, and previews whatever is selected. It is not a floating window: it is a child of the Explorer tab, so it moves with it, is clipped to it and, if you want, shrinks the Details columns to reserve its own space, the way File Pilot's inspector does.

Folders open with Explorer's own file list, not a copy: the same icons, columns, sorting, view modes and scrollbars. Text, images, video, audio, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, archives and everything else have their own preview or a proper fallback. Nothing runs on a timer in the background, and nothing that touches the disk ever blocks Explorer.

Highlights

  • A panel, not a window. Space opens it, Space or Esc closes it, the header has a close button for the mouse. It docks on the right, or at the bottom when the window is too narrow; drag its edge to change its width and the width is remembered.
  • Folders, with Explorer's own list. The preview hosts a real Explorer browser, so icons, columns, sorting, grouping and the Details / List / Icons view modes are Explorer's. A view dropdown in the header switches between Details, List, Small, Medium, Large and Extra Large icons.
  • A real filter, at the same level. Typing in the filter box shows only the matching direct children of the previewed folder, with their original columns, and clearing it brings the folder back. No subfolder is ever searched.
  • Text and code, detected by content. No extension list: a file is text when its bytes say so, so .ahk, .psd1, .config, extensionless files and anything else just work. UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE and the ANSI code page are decoded, and the footer reports which one was used, the size and the line count.
  • An editor-style toolbar. Word wrap, line numbers (a wrapped continuation keeps its number once), a whitespace inspector that draws spaces as dim dots, and alternating row colors. The four toggles are remembered if you want them remembered, and the defaults are settings.
  • Search inside the file. The same filter box keeps only the matching lines, each with its original line number, and highlights every match with your Windows accent color.
  • Documents without Office. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF and OpenDocument files are opened as a zip of XML parts and reduced to their text, so they preview instantly even when Office is not installed. Old binary .doc, .xls and .ppt files use the Windows preview handler when one is registered.
  • Images, video and audio. Images are decoded at full resolution, videos show a frame and audio shows its album art, both through the same still-image providers Windows uses.
  • PDF. Rendered by the Windows PDF preview handler, the same component Explorer's preview pane uses, hosted inside the panel. Zoom and scroll belong to the handler.
  • Archives. A .zip (and any format the shell exposes as a folder) lists its contents in the native list. Formats with no shell namespace fall back to the properties view.
  • A fallback that still helps. Anything else shows the real file icon plus its type, size, modified date and full path.
  • Colors that follow Windows. The panel samples Explorer's actual pixels for the background and the text, and takes the accent from Windows itself, so light, dark and custom accents look native.
  • Explorer never freezes. Listing a folder, reading a file, decoding an image, building a thumbnail or checking a cloud placeholder all run on worker threads. The panel opens at once with a loading state, a new selection cancels the previous load, and a file that is only a cloud placeholder is never downloaded just to be previewed.

A few of the things it previews:

Install

  1. Install Windhawk (Windows 10 or 11).
  2. Open Quick Look on windhawk.net and press Install.
  3. Select a file or folder in File Explorer and press Space.

Quick Look is an injected mod: it runs inside explorer.exe, which is what lets the panel be a real child of the window instead of a window that follows it.

Keys

Key Action
Space Open or close the preview
Esc Close the preview
Click the close button Close the preview with the mouse
Shift + wheel Scroll a text preview sideways when word wrap is off
Mouse wheel / drag the bars Scroll the preview

Settings

Setting Default What it does
Shrink columns to fit the panel On Shrinks the file view and scales the Details columns to the space left by the panel. Turn it off to overlay the panel instead.
Remember the text preview options On Keeps wrap, line numbers, whitespace dots and alternating rows as you left them for the next window or session.
Line numbers by default Off The gutter used when the options are not remembered.
Alternating rows by default Off The alternating row color used when the options are not remembered.

What each file shows

Selection Preview
Folder Explorer's native list, with a view dropdown, a name filter and file/folder counts
Text, code, config, logs Text with wrap, line numbers, whitespace dots, alternating rows and in-file search
Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF, OpenDocument The document text, read directly without Office
Old .doc, .xls, .ppt The Windows preview handler when one is installed, otherwise the properties view
Images (png, jpg, gif, bmp, tif, ico, webp…) The decoded image, fitted to the panel
Video and audio A frame or the album art, as Windows produces it
PDF The Windows PDF preview handler, hosted in the panel
Archives (.zip, and formats with a shell namespace) The archive contents in the native list
Anything else The real file icon with type, size, modified date and path

How it behaves

  • The panel never navigates. Double-clicking a folder inside the preview opens its Properties; it does not enter it. Quick Look is a preview, not a file manager.
  • Single click selects. A double click on empty space does nothing.
  • Cloud files are left alone. A file that is only a placeholder is not downloaded to be previewed.
  • Text is capped. A text preview reads the first 200 KB and says so in the footer.

Troubleshooting

  • Space does nothing. The panel only opens when the file list itself has the focus, so a pending rename, an address bar edit or the search box is never hijacked. Click the file list and try again.
  • Something looks wrong. Turn on the Windhawk log for this mod (Advanced tab), reproduce it and attach the log to the issue. It is off by default because it adds a line for every step.
  • A document shows only text. That is by design: modern Office and OpenDocument files are read as text, so layout, images and colors are not part of the preview.

Contributing

Bug reports, fixes and new features are welcome. Open an issue with your Windows build, the mod version, the steps to reproduce it and, when it is visual, a screenshot or a short clip.

For a pull request: fork the repository, branch from main, change quick-look.wh.cpp, confirm it compiles and open the PR describing what changed and why. One bug or feature per PR is much easier to review.

License

Released under the MIT License. See the license file. The inflate code that reads Word and OpenDocument files is derived from zlib's puff.c and keeps its zlib license notice in the source.

entry.title: PWA Tray Center 0.5.610
entry.content:
PWA Tray Center

Adds a "Hide to PWA Tray Center" item to the window menu of installed Chrome PWA windows (right-click title bar).

  • Hidden windows keep running (music plays, etc.)
  • One tray icon for all PWAs. By default it stays in the tray. With Always show tray icon turned off (Settings → Advanced), it appears only while PWAs are hidden and disappears when the last one is restored

Tray Icon

  • Left click → opens PWA Tray Center (Fluent flyout, rounded corners, Mica or solid backdrop, chosen in Settings)
  • Right click → menu: Show all / Quit all
  • Center mode (Settings → Panel): Hermes (Quick) closes on a click outside, Titan (Pinned) stays open

Tabs

Tab Description
Media Cards for each Chrome media session: cover, title, artist, PWA source, prev/play-pause/next, draggable progress bar. Right-click for controls. Cover style (small, full or none) and compact view (3 covers per row) are set in Settings.
Apps Hidden PWAs. Left-click to show, right-click for Show/Quit. Badge shows unread counter.
Notifications Toast notifications from Windows notification center. Falls back to unread counter from window title (e.g. (3) Inbox).
Library All installed Chrome PWAs. Left-click to launch/show. Drag to reorder. Right-click for Open/Quit/categories. Search field + category chips for filtering.
Settings All mod options (Panel, Media, PWAs, Notifications, Advanced). No Windhawk settings needed.

Tabs, cards, and tiles are drag-to-reorder; order is remembered.

Notifications are not verified yet and may not work.

Technical Notes

  • Only affects PWA windows (identified by AppUserModelID with _crx_<app id>)
  • Regular browser windows and other programs are untouched
  • Library reads from Chrome's Web Applications folders (default or --user-data-dir)

Chrome Volume

Volume bar in Media tab controls Chrome's system-wide volume (same as Windows volume mixer). Dims when no audio session; changes apply when Chrome starts playing. It can be turned on or off in Settings. The level stays as set after the mod is disabled.

Limitations

  • Does not keep PWA alive after browser process exits
  • Audio may stop if browser freezes or discards background pages (Memory Saver / Efficiency mode)

entry.title: Middle Click Minimize 1.1.3
entry.content:
Middle Click Minimize

This mod allows you to minimize windows by middle-clicking (using the scroll wheel) directly on the title bar.

Exclusions and Conflicts

  • How to exclude programs: To disable the mod for a specific program (e.g., steam.exe or vivaldi.exe), add it to the custom process exclusion list in the mod's Advanced tab in Windhawk.
  • Known conflicts: If you use the "Middle-Click New Tab Chrome/Edge/Brave" mod, middle-clicking the empty tab-strip might minimize the browser instead of opening a new tab. You can add your browser to the exclusion list in the Advanced tab to prevent this.

entry.title: WinTips OSD 1.5.2
entry.content:
• Added an input language tip: Win+Space, Ctrl+Shift, Alt+Shift and Shift inside an IME now show the input language, or the Chinese/English mode inside a Chinese IME. Off by default.
  • The backdrop now keeps refreshing while the card is up (Windows 10 2004 and later), so a video or a scrolling page moves through the blur instead of freezing on the frame it had when the tip appeared. The card excludes itself from its own screen grabs, so it is not picked up by screenshots and recordings while it is visible.
  • Keys pressed while an administrator window has focus now come from Raw Input, which covers Insert and copy/paste/cut there too, not just the lock keys. The key-state poll stays behind it for remote sessions and virtual keyboards. The "Detect toggles under elevated apps" setting is gone: the integrity level of the foreground process is read instead, and the fallback only runs when it is actually needed.
  • Added a topmost guard: a fullscreen game, a recorder or a launcher overlay covering the card is noticed within 100 ms and the card is raised again. When nothing covers it, no other window is touched.
  • The settings page no longer has "Detect toggles under elevated apps"; nothing else was renamed, so existing settings carry over.
  • Rewrote the mod description.

entry.title: Desktop Icons Proximity Reveal 1.0.3
entry.content:
Desktop Icons Proximity Reveal

Hide desktop icons when you are not using them. Hover near an icon or over a custom area to fade them back in.

Features:

  • Draw up to 32 reveal areas around your icons.
  • Reveal each group separately, or show all icons together.
  • Adjust fade speed, hide delay, and hover padding.
  • Preview your areas and save them between sessions.
  • Keep new folders and shortcuts visible while naming them, then hide them after an outside click or a configurable timeout (15 seconds by default).
  • Selected icons stay visible until deselected; press Ctrl+A to reveal all. Disable Keep selected icons visible to turn this off.
  • Keep icons permanently visible using Always-visible icons (whitelist). Enter desktop names separated by semicolons, such as Recycle Bin; Steam; Discord. Names ignore case; * and ? wildcards are supported.

Setup

  1. Enable Show box editor panel in Settings and apply.
  2. Click Edit boxes. All icons appear, including those outside saved areas. Drag around your icons to add areas.
  3. Click Save & apply or Cancel to restore normal hiding. Switch the panel setting off to close it.

The panel stays closed at startup. If its setting is already on, switch it off and on again to reopen it.

Separate groups are enabled by default. Without active areas, hovering near any icon shows all icons. Recycle Bin and folders work too.

How this differs from other mods

Desktop Icon Section Auto-Hide uses a single section or box. This mod adds up to 32 separately animated areas, a drag-to-draw editor, and temporary visibility for newly created items. Flashlight Desktop Icons and Spotlight reveal icons near the cursor rather than inside saved groups. Smooth Desktop Icons Auto-Hide and ZenDesktop focus on hiding and restoring the desktop as a whole.

Note: Requires Windows 10/11 x64. Keep Windows' Show desktop icons enabled. Hidden icons retain their Windows click targets; icons outside all boxes stay hidden unless selected, whitelisted, temporarily revealed, or accessed by keyboard. Redraw areas after changing monitors; avoid running other icon hiding mods.

Rendering hooks adapted from Desktop Icons Transparency by zed712969-crypto.

entry.title: Gradual Night Light 0.4.2
entry.content:
Gradual Night Light

Automatically adjust Windows' native Night light throughout the evening, with an editable daily schedule and optional gradual transitions.

Default schedule

Setting Time Strength
Stage 1 19:00 50
Stage 2 20:00 60
Stage 3 21:00 70
Off time 07:00 Off

Settings

  • Off time: the local time when Night light turns off each day.
  • Stages: add or remove stages with Windhawk's list controls. Each stage has a time and a strength from 1 (weakest) to 100 (warmest). Three stages are provided by default; between 1 and 96 stages are supported.
  • Gradual transitions: interpolate strength between stages. For example, the default schedule produces strength 55 at 19:30. Disable this option to change strength only at each stage's start time.

Times use the local 24-hour HH:MM format. Stages are sorted automatically and the schedule repeats daily, including across midnight. All stage times must be unique and different from Off time. Invalid settings are reported in the mod log; an invalid edit keeps the last valid configuration. If saved settings are invalid at startup, the tool stays running without applying a schedule until valid settings are saved.

Night light switches off at Off time and stays off until the next stage. The last stage holds its strength until Off time. To fade in from almost no warmth, add a stage such as 18:30 with strength 1 before 19:00 with strength 50. Add further stages to create a five-stage schedule or a gradual morning fade.

Behavior and restoration

The scheduler runs in a dedicated Windhawk tool process. Every ten seconds it applies the scheduled temperature directly through Windows' display pipeline. It also checks after display changes, resume, and session unlock.

Settings and Quick Settings show Windows' own Night light configuration. Windows continues running its own schedule in the background. Its transitions can briefly take precedence until the next mod check. The mod pauses while Windows previews its strength slider. Disabling the mod reapplies the temperature requested by Windows' current settings.

The mod reads the current user's Night light settings and state from CloudStore. It applies all scheduled changes at runtime without writing either record. If Windhawk is terminated during a stage, the runtime tint may last until Windows next applies Night light or the user signs out.

If you tested an earlier prerelease, disable it before upgrading so that version can restore the settings it saved.

Requirements and limitations

The mod uses internal Windows Night light display interfaces and the modern CloudStore Current layout. The display driver must support Night light. The tool launcher supports Windhawk 1.7.3 and newer. The runtime interfaces were tested on Windows 11 build 26100, x64, with two displays. HDR and ARM64 have not been verified. If records are missing, open Settings > System > Display > Night light once.

Technical references

The parser and scheduler are independently implemented using the documented research below. No external helper, script, or runtime download is required.

  • Night light registry format research
  • Microsoft Bond CompactBinary protocol
  • Official Windhawk tool mod launcher

entry.title: Floating Taskbar 2.1.13
entry.content:
Floating Taskbar

Left-aligned taskbar layout with the default gradient background.

Features

  • Configure the floating bar width, taskbar area height, bottom gap, and corner radii.
  • Configure the corner radius of taskbar hover highlights.
  • Use the system background, a transparent background, translucent color, a solid color, a linear gradient, or a custom XAML brush.
  • Click through blank areas inside the floating taskbar.
  • Keep tray menus and Quick Settings aligned with the right edge of the bar.

Settings

Widths, area height, spacing, and radii are physical pixels. A taskbar area height of 0 follows the system. A custom XAML background that is left empty also follows the system background.

The same physical-pixel values appear differently at different display scales. Set the values separately if precise consistency across mixed-DPI monitors is required.

Multi-window taskbar highlights are currently detected from the Chinese and English taskbar accessible names. On other Windows display languages, those highlights may not be hidden.

Differences from other mods

Windows 11 Taskbar Styler, Taskbar height and icon size, and MacOS Style Dock can also create a floating or unusually sized taskbar. Floating Taskbar also adds click-through blank space, tray and Quick Settings alignment, automatic tray layout reassertion, and multi-window highlight cleanup. It writes properties on the taskbar's RootGrid and BackgroundFill, so combining it with a Taskbar Styler theme that styles the same properties is not supported.

Use Windhawk's normal mod toggle to disable the mod; there is no separate enable setting.

中文说明

将 Windows 11 任务栏变为独立的悬浮圆角条，可调整长度、区域高度、悬浮间距、 任务栏与待选框圆角，以及背景颜色或渐变。悬浮条内部空白区域可以点击穿透， 托盘菜单与快速设置面板会对齐悬浮条右端。

长度、区域高度、间距和圆角使用物理像素。多窗口任务栏高亮目前依靠中文或英文 辅助功能名称识别，其他显示语言可能不隐藏该高亮。若同时使用 Taskbar Styler 并修改相同的 RootGrid 或 BackgroundFill 属性，两个 Mod 可能冲突。

entry.title: WinPager 0.1.2
entry.content:
WinPager

A virtual desktop pager like KDE Plasma's, living in the Windows 11 taskbar.

  • Shows every virtual desktop with live window outlines, optionally with application icons
  • Click a desktop to switch to it; click the current one to open Task View (configurable)
  • Scroll over it to flip through desktops
  • Drag a window outline onto another desktop to move that window there
  • Hover a desktop for a list of its windows; right-click to add or remove desktops
  • Ctrl+Shift+Win+Left/Right moves the active window to the neighbouring desktop and follows it
  • KWin-style on-screen display when switching, and an option to hide Windows' own "Desktop N" popup
  • A pager on each monitor's taskbar, or one on the main taskbar showing all monitors
  • Can show only a few desktops at a time, scrolling along with the current one
  • Follows light/dark mode and the accent color

The settings mirror those of Plasma's Pager widget, plus position, theme and the switching popups.

The mod runs in its own process; it isn't injected into explorer.exe.

Notes

  • Windows 11 24H2/25H2 (build 26100 and later) only. Like other virtual desktop tools, it relies on undocumented virtual desktop interfaces, so a Windows update can break it. On a build it doesn't know, it shows an error.
  • The taskbar doesn't reserve space for it. Next to a centered row of buttons it shows only as many desktops as fit (at least the current one); on a left-aligned taskbar, a row of buttons long enough to reach the tray runs under it.
  • With "Hide the Windows "Desktop N" popup" on, a volume or brightness popup shown within 0.6 s of a switch is hidden too, since Explorer shows both in the same window.
  • WinPager is also a standalone app, WinPager.exe, built from the same source. Only one of the two runs at a time: if you switch to the mod, quit WinPager.exe and turn off its "Start with Windows".
  • Bugs and ideas: github.com/seanmamasde/WinPager/issues

entry.title: Windows 7 Desktop Widgets 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Added authentic Windows 7 CPU & RAM Meter gadget with compact and large modes.
  • Implemented real-time CPU and RAM usage sampling with smooth damped needle physics.
  • 100% pure vector GDI+ rendering (no external image dependencies).
  • Fully updated settings descriptions and metadata to English.
  • Enhanced multi-monitor DPI scaling and border click-through.

entry.title: Round Everything Interface 2.0.0
entry.content:
• Renamed to Round Everything Interface (the id stays round-everything; installed copies keep running)
  • Themes: Solid (default), Tape, Frost, Bleed, Windows, Eclipse, Phantom, Neon and Custom - each sets the frame, fill, bevel, shadow, monitor corners and the dwm.exe window options; their frame fill and edge line follow the Windows mode, in the colors of Windows' own taskbar with transparency effects off (#EEEEEE|#1C1C1C, #BEBEBE|#404040), unless the theme has colors of its own. A few Overrides (frame thickness, screen radius, monitor corner radius, frame color, gradient angle and color source, fill, work-area inset, window radius) apply on top of any theme
  • Settings reorganized into Theme / Overrides / General / Custom theme groups; values saved by 1.0.0 under keys that changed fall back to their defaults. Per-edge thickness overrides moved to a new key (edgeOffsetsClockwise, taskbar's edge first, then clockwise) so 1.0.0's left,top,right,bottom values aren't read in the new order. "Inward offset" is now "Frame thickness", and the monitor corners are one radius setting (0 turns them off)
  • Applying a theme logs its values, with the General and Overrides groups, as the mod's settings in Windhawk's JSON form, in rows broken between values so a column selection copies them whole - ready to paste and tweak as the Custom theme
  • Frame color: one color, a gradient of several at a set angle, or a light|dark pair following the Windows mode (each side may be a gradient); "accent" (or an empty color) is the Windows accent in a shade that keeps the taskbar readable - SystemAccentColorDark2 on a dark taskbar, SystemAccentColorLight2 on a light one - and follows the accent and the mode as they change
  • Fills: Solid; Custom acrylic (live DWM blur through Windows.UI.Composition, with blur, tint, luminosity, saturation and noise); Windows' default (the taskbar's own light or dark acrylic, following the Windows mode). A gradient frame color fills the solid frame and feeds the acrylic's tint and luminosity. The effect graph holds only the effects that change something. Falls back to a layered frame if composition can't be set up
  • One frame, one piece: every fill is the same composition window, under the taskbar too (the taskbar's background is made transparent), so the bevel, edge line and corner arcs run along the taskbar's edge as along the others
  • Like Windows' own acrylic, the acrylic fills turn solid while transparency effects are off, and while battery saver is on (the "Solid while battery saver is on" setting, on by default)
  • Acrylic glass bevel along the inner edge (two lights, specular, Fresnel, an edge line in its own color, edge shade), rasterized once with the frame; its strengths and the edge line color take a light|dark pair following the Windows mode, and the edge line color "accent" too. The edge line shows its color exactly: at full strength it covers the frame's innermost pixel row
  • Inner shadow along the rounded screen (blur, opacity, color, offsets); the color takes "accent" or a light|dark pair too
  • One-pixel bezel ring along all four screen edges, inside the taskbar too, also with monitor corners off; the frame thickness is measured from inside it. It stays on screen while the frame re-shapes (a settings change, the taskbar moving)
  • Frame color source "Title bar": the frame takes the color of the maximized window's title bar - its fourth row inside the rounded screen, past the inner shadow, read off the screen the way Top Taskbar Bleed reads it (the app is never asked to render), dominant color, columns under a dialog or flyout left out, nothing read while a thumbnail preview shows or while a window is still zooming in or out. A window seen before gets its last color at once; otherwise the row is read every frame until two readings agree, and the frame eases to it over 350 ms. Hovering a thumbnail until Aero Peek shows a maximized window gives the frame that window's color. Each taskbar switches to the light or dark theme to stay readable (per taskbar, via RequestedTheme; the approach is Top Taskbar Bleed's)
  • The work area is always shrunk to the rounded screen (the option is gone), so nothing hides under the frame
  • Auto-hide taskbar supported: the frame and the work area stay exactly as with the taskbar docked and the taskbar slides over its band; the mod keeps its own appbar over the taskbar's strip, so toggling auto-hide moves no window
  • With Monitors set to the primary one, the other monitors' taskbars are handed back and their windows keep Windows' corners, border and shadow
  • dwm.exe: one Window corner radius setting (-1 Windows' own, 0 square, else the radius, maximized windows included); border and shadow on maximized windows - the shadow on the topmost maximized window per monitor only, styles learned from DWM's own calls; custom active/inactive border colors with opacity, defaulting to the accent (active) and #3C3C3C (inactive), each also a light|dark pair following the app mode; stays out of dwm.exe after two DWM restarts within a minute of its own load
  • dwm.exe: corners stay rounded through maximize, snap and restore animations - DWM's animation clip, which it eases to square, keeps the radius, and on a restore the window being stretched into place has its own clip fitted to the stretch, so its corners don't widen (the clip's geometry is tracked through its destructor; where that can't be hooked, a restore keeps Windows' stretched corner)
  • dwm.exe: apps that draw their whole frame themselves, which Windows leaves square (Autodesk AutoCAD 2013, Design Review), are rounded too - "Round apps Windows leaves square" under General, on by default; maximized, their border and clip are cut to the work area, and they stay rounded while AltSnap drags them see-through
  • dwm.exe: the accent border color follows the user's accent as it changes - dwm.exe runs under an account of its own, so the explorer.exe part publishes the accent and the app mode - and maximized windows get Windows' accent border only while "Show accent color on title bars and window borders" is on
  • Sturdier against Windows updates: every udwm.dll and taskbar.dll symbol is optional, and one an update renames or drops costs only the feature that uses it (logged by name), with fallbacks for the window radius and the taskbar lookup
  • Fix: maximized windows' shadows stacked - the windows that don't hold the shadow now get DWM's own no-shadow style
  • Fix: maximized windows sometimes came up without their border - a border update DWM makes without asking for the corner radius first now finds the window maximized all the same
  • Fix: with Windows' accent option off, maximized windows could pick up an accent border learned from apps that color their own border
  • Fix: with a full-screen screen recorder running, the frame covered the taskbar's icons; it now follows the taskbar down when the shell demotes it
  • Fix: clicking a grouped taskbar button hid the frame until its thumbnail flyout closed
  • Fix: the bezel ring was missing along the taskbar's two ends
  • Fix: saving a setting flashed the bezel ring white for a frame or two
  • Fix: the edge line showed lighter or darker than its color - it reached its pixel row at three quarters strength, letting the frame or the content behind show through
  • Fix: dragging a window under the acrylic frame stuttered (the frame is composed at alpha 255; 254 made DWM render it through a monitor-sized intermediate surface every frame)
  • Fix: content DWM changed behind the frame by itself (a minimized window's last image, a shadow after a handover) stayed in the bands; invisible layered windows under each band are repainted on window events so DWM re-reads the backdrop
  • Fix: the ArtCraft apps (PhotoCraft and the rest), which drop the caption while maximized, covered the whole monitor and were taken for full-screen apps - the taskbar dropped behind them and Do not disturb came on. Those apps, told by their program, are now moved to the work area once per maximize; other apps that maximize the same way are left as they are
  • Fix: screen capture and color picker overlays (ShareX, Snipping Tool, PowerToys Color Picker and others) were taken for full-screen apps and hid the frame they were capturing
  • Fix: Show desktop briefly stretches a secondary taskbar's window over its monitor, and the frame on that monitor was torn down and rebuilt; a taskbar window covering its monitor now keeps the strip it was on, and the frame stays

entry.title: Windows 7/8/8.1 Taskbar Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 7/8/8.1 Taskbar Recreation

This mod recreates taskbars inspired by Windows 7, Windows 8 and Windows 8.1 on Windows 10 and 11. The taskbar runs in a dedicated Explorer process on a best-effort basis. Appearance and behavior can vary with the Windows build, DPI, taskbar replacement and other shell mods.

Features

  • Four skin presets: Windows 7, Windows 8 Beta 8148, Windows 8.0 and Windows 8.1, plus Custom for individual Start options.
  • Task buttons, window previews, Jump Lists, notification icons and toolbars.
  • An integrated notification area and taskbar, with a fallback to the native bar if the integrated tray cannot start.
  • Horizontal and vertical layouts, Aero Peek and classic flyout options.
  • Change notification area icon visibility using the Control Panel page that the mod attempts to restore, including on Windows 11; availability and behavior can vary.
  • Static taskbar textures and system colors; the textures do not blur live windows behind the bar. Windows 7 skin adds a cursor-following, icon-colored hover glow for running apps.
  • Local taskbar pins and ordering: the mod does not change Windows pins. Drag to an empty task area to pin; hover a running app to activate its window.
  • An advanced battery flyout option; compatibility may vary between Windows builds.
  • Optional secondary taskbars show pins, windows and the shared private tray. Secondary AppBar registration reserves work area when necessary and allowed by the shell. DPI scaling and flyout positioning are best-effort.
  • Experimental shell minimize-rectangle support supplies reconstructed button coordinates to Windows, without changing Windows 7 Window Animations Restorer. Availability depends on Windows shell-hook delivery and ordering.
  • Optional icon-only horizontal button width: native default, manual logical width, or read-only following of Taskbar height and icon size for standard registry-based Windhawk installations. This does not change icon size or taskbar height and does not hook or modify the other mod. Unsupported installation layouts use the original width.

Themes

Windows 7

Windows 8 Beta 8148

Windows 8.0

Windows 8.1

Custom

Choose individual Start options instead of a preset.

Installation

  1. Install and enable the mod in Windhawk.
  2. Choose a skin preset in the mod settings.
  3. Restart the mod after changing settings that require it.

Settings

The mod settings control the skin, Start button, taskbar layout, notification area, previews, flyouts and other behavior. Individual descriptions in Windhawk explain their scope and any restart requirements.

Behavior and limitations

  • The taskbar runs in a separate explorer.exe process on a best-effort basis. Notification-page hooks still run in Explorer, and other Explorer mods can load in the separate process. A watchdog attempts to restore the native taskbar after an unexpected exit; recovery from a hang or other failure is not guaranteed.

  • Skins are approximations; Windows 7 popup frames use the current system's DWM frame when available.

  • The Windows 8 Start corner is illustrated, not a live Start-screen preview.

  • Vertical layout, Aero Peek and classic flyouts may vary between Windows builds.

  • On first use, the mod downloads pnidui.dll, SndVolSSO.dll and batmeter.dll. The advanced battery flyout also downloads stobject.dll and an English or Italian language-pack CAB. Downloaded files are checked against pinned SHA-256 hashes. The Windows 10 1511 stobject.dll is loaded into the dedicated tool process and stays loaded until that process exits.

  • The integrated tray is enabled by default. It creates a private Shell_TrayWnd host and hides the native taskbar. Applications and mods that find the taskbar by class can encounter the private host; tray and AppBar traffic routed to it is processed or forwarded by the mod's UI thread. The host supplies taskbar geometry and forwards wheel input in supported cases, but it does not contain the native taskbar's ReBarWindow32, MSTaskSwWClass, Start button or XAML content. Mods that depend on those windows or content can fail or conflict. Disable the integrated tray and reload the mod if this compatibility trade-off is unsuitable.

  • The integrated tray keeps “Always show all icons” in memory for the current session. It starts from the Windows preference and does not write that preference to the system registry; it is reset when the mod reloads.

  • The Notification Area Icons page uses a private COM provider. The mod attempts to close its hosting window before unloading the Explorer hooks. Behavior has not been verified on every Windows build; if the window cannot be identified or does not respond, close the page before disabling, updating, or reloading the mod.

  • Keep a way to disable the mod or restart Explorer.

  • Windows 11 Taskbar Styler and its skins are technical references; their authors are not involved in this mod.

Credits

  • WinBoeing777 - Testing on Windows 10 22H2 and Suggestions
  • Cips - Testing on Windows 11 25H2
  • Kiyaku - Suggestions and Testing

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 3.1.1
entry.content:
Fixes

  • The island no longer crashes inside Windows' media controls while media apps or a browser's videos (like YouTube in Chrome) keep changing: a media session that goes away (or stops being the one shown) is kept with its handlers for 10 seconds before the media thread lets it go, since Windows may still be calling it on its own threads (also when the media thread stops, without keeping the island waiting). If the island's process ever crashes (an NTSTATUS exit code), the explorer part starts it again, at most 3 times in 10 minutes, and only when it was Windhawk's own windhawk.exe at Explorer's integrity level (decided at its hello, while it runs), launched with CreateProcessInternalW like the tool mod snippet. On Windhawk 2.0 the island runs in windhawk-mod.exe, which Windhawk starts itself, so the mod doesn't start it again there.
  • With the Fixed style's notches minimized, a notification's app icon peeks out only of the notch with the bell, not out of every notch, and no longer for the app you're using (a taskbar badge from the app in front).
  • A click on a notification opens its app when the app's own notification handler doesn't answer (its COM activation fails within 5 seconds), instead of doing nothing: the island falls back to the app's window, its tray icon or the app itself.
  • An app's own counter on its taskbar button (like WhatsApp's) no longer keeps its icon on the island as a waiting notification while the list is empty ("No notifications", so no "Clear all" to dismiss it): it counts as seen when the app comes to the front (or is in front when it changes) or its icon on the island is clicked, and shows again when the counter goes away and comes back or its number grows.
  • Sleep in the power button's menu no longer hibernates PCs with Modern Standby: with no S1-S3, it turns the screen off like Start > Sleep instead of calling SetSuspendState.
  • QQ's and WeChat's message preview shows again when hovering their icon in the taskbar's tray with tray icons on the island: the island answers Shell_NotifyIconGetRect with its own place only while the mouse is on that icon on the island (#7157).
  • The settings window takes much less of the processor in its first seconds: the preview's hint, the "+ Line" glow and the other hints that only fade or pulse draw at most 30 times a second instead of at the monitor's rate.
  • Dock: games' icons (like Steam's) and other apps without an icon of their own in the Start menu no longer go empty when Windows' icon cache is out of date (an empty picture now counts as none and the next source is tried), nor show a small icon magnified: the last fallback reads the window's program's icon from the file as big as the dock shows it, before the window's own 32 px icon (#7207).
  • Right after a Windows update whose taskbar.dll symbols Microsoft hasn't published yet (KB5132061, taskbar.dll 10.0.26100.9974, was 🔴 on the symbol cache's status page), the explorer part no longer stops as a whole. ExplorerModInit returned FALSE when HookTaskbarDllSymbols failed, so the island lost its tray icons too, which need no symbols (subclass and WM_COPYDATA). Now the taskbar stays as Windows draws it (g_taskbarSymbols false: no symbol hook is set, and GetTaskbarXamlRoot/GetSecondaryTaskbarXamlRoot return null instead of calling a symbol pointer), ApplyToTaskbar counts the main taskbar as ready so the late start goes on, and the tray icons and the apps asking for attention keep reaching the island. The explorer part keeps the taskbar.dll version without symbols in the mod's storage (taskbarNoSymbols, cleared once they load), and the main island shows a sticky notice saying why, once per version and only when the chosen taskbar needs them (the dock, the transparent taskbar, only the apps, or the tray hidden). Its "Details" button, or a click on it, opens the island's What's new, where this fix tells why (the whole text may not fit a smaller notice). The dock comes back once the symbols are published and load with Explorer (its next start). Without taskbar.dll at all, it still returns FALSE.
  • The islands no longer stall every few seconds on PCs with apps chosen for the visualizer (since 3.1). Each island, every 3 s, read all the default output's audio sessions again once per chosen app, each read making a new IAudioSessionManager2, asking for every session's state and process and opening each program (~12 ms a read), all on the islands' thread: with 8 apps on 3 islands a tick took 30 ms to over a second, found with a per-message timing log and by sampling the thread. Now one list (g_audioSessions) is read at most every 1.5 s for every island and app, the output's session manager is kept (made again for another default output or after a failure), each program's file is looked up once per process, and the list is released with the islands, before CoUninitialize.
